content:
This thread tracks the progress of deprecating Valued from Mathlib.
A Valued instance will be replaced by [ValuativeRel R] [UniformSpace R] [IsValuativeTopology R] [IsUniformAddGroup R] (v : Valuation R A) [v.Compatible].

The refactor progress:

  1. Copy APIs that take Valued as input and make them accept input [ValuativeRel R] [UniformSpace R] [IsValuativeTopology R] [IsUniformAddGroup R] (v : Valuation R A) [v.Compatible].
  • [merged] #36532 [APIs in Valued.ValuativeRel and Valued.ValuationTopology are now generalized and copied into ValuativeRel.ValuativeTopology.]

  1. For every API that introduces a Valued instance, copy that API and make it create [ValuativeRel R] [UniformSpace R] [IsValuativeTopology R] [IsUniformAddGroup R] instances. And for every instance that currently exists in Mathlib, create the above series of instances as much as possible without introducing diamonds.
    More specifically, currently in Mathlib, there are three main ways of creating a Valued instance:

    • Valued.mk'
    • Valued.valuedCompletion
    • NormedField.toValued

    For each of these we create APIs to create the above series of instances.

  • [WIP] #36769 [APIs related toValued.valuedCompletion. The completion of valuations.]
  1. A big PR deprecating the Valued class using 1 and 2.

-1. Solving problems encountered during refactoring.

  • [ready] #36777 [Generalize the definition of IsValuativeTopology to non comm rings, ensuring future APIs don't lose mathematical content.]
  • [blocked] #36911 [change ValueGroup from taking HomClass to Hom, fixing erw and transparency problems]

In the preparation of #36769, I realized the we only have the extension of valuation to completion of valued fields now. But mathematically we can do this for arbitrary rings with topology compatible valuation. I'll try to implement it in #36769.
I've left three small comments, if the bench results are OK then #36777 is ready to go.
The results are not very good... anyone wants to understand what's happening?

Re #36777 - I can take a look but can someone offer me a good answer to why we want valuations on non-commutative rings other than "the axioms happen to make sense in this generality"? Is there an example in nature?
I was also puzzled by this, but it seems they are a thing
anyway the bench is now good, so we don't need to worry about "a maybe useless and costly generalization"

It is somewhat my fault since I insisted with Jiedong to generalise: the point is that they play a big role in noncommutative Iwasawa theory, where Iwasawa algebras are often studied through valuations induced by the (uniform) ppp-adic group in the sense of Lazard.
With great help from @Edison Xie , now #36769 and #40309 are ready for review.
Note that the above two PRs are the only PRs remained before the big total deprecation PR of Valued from mathlib.
Both #36769 and #40309 are ready for review again.
